bounded_residuals.bounded_handling: Use an idempotent receipt/reconciliation keyed by release hash and destination inode, or require explicit manual reconciliation of an incomplete receipt before retry.
bounded_residuals.evidence: A crash after path.rename and before receipt append/save leaves a moved item in the target without a move record; rerun rejects the existing target at line 33 and has no reconciliation path.
bounded_residuals.impact: The item remains recoverable in Trash, but the operation is left partially recorded and cannot resume through this script.

coverage_limitations: Static source and current ignored selection only; no execution, dry-run, mutation, or new tests. Current review applies only to the exact target SHA above.

findings.closure: Replace safety asserts with explicit fail-closed conditionals/raises and reject optimized mode at startup. Verify no side effects in optimized mode without invoking real move paths.
findings.evidence: All authorization, path-confinement, nested-path, reference, and pre/post-rename safety checks are Python assert statements.
findings.impact: Python optimization (`-O` / PYTHONOPTIMIZE) removes every assert. In that mode the release path and candidate paths can reach target.mkdir/path.rename without the guards; a crafted trash_directory_name can also escape .Trash.

findings.closure: Keep source extractions preserve-only unless each tree is content-bound to an exact retained source archive/distribution and its owner confirms no remaining consumer; add an explicit category allowlist matching the user-authorized set.
findings.evidence: The current selection contains 23 `source_archive_extraction` candidates. The mover has no category allowlist and treats a released path as eligible after status flags; its checks establish only sibling archive/distribution path existence, not tree identity or content equality.
findings.impact: An editable extraction with unique changes or a live consumer could be moved under an authorization string limited to repeatable test directories and used environments. A retained candidate.tar does not preserve edits made after extraction.

findings.closure: Bind the selection to its source inventory hash; require release roots to equal that inventory’s exact admitted C-root set; validate every path component with lstat from a trusted nonsymlink root through candidate and Trash.
findings.evidence: The selection source inventory path/SHA is not loaded or checked. Owner membership is checked only against roots supplied by release JSON, and path confinement is only the broad `.codex/worktrees` prefix. The parent-symlink loop breaks at owner.parent before lstat-checking that component or higher ancestors.
findings.impact: A malformed or re-authored selection/release can broaden the move beyond the 14 admitted C roots. A symlinked owner.parent can redirect candidate lstat/rename through an outside target while lexical `is_relative_to` checks still pass.

findings.closure: Compile the release input root-only from the exact expected topic/audit set after status checks; require the complete set and bind every required handoff/deciding output ref to a frozen branch/HEAD and its SHA/byte count.
findings.evidence: Audit completion and committed-work claims are booleans in release JSON. Git refs are checked for retrievable bytes/hash but only required to be nonempty; `frozen_topics` can be empty or omit topics, and refs are not tied to a complete expected topic/evidence set or proven reachable from each frozen topic head.
findings.impact: The code can pass a partial or unrelated evidence list while asserting that all deciding outputs/useful changes and audits are complete.

findings.closure: Require a new unique receipt path below the exact cleanup directory, reject overlap with candidate/preserve paths, verify nonsymlink ancestors, and create exclusively before using an atomic same-directory update strategy.
findings.evidence: `output_path` is caller-controlled and `save()` unconditionally uses write_text, truncating any existing file; the path is not confined to cleanup scratch or checked against candidates/preserve refs.
findings.impact: A path/argument mistake can overwrite an existing probe, receipt, source file, or other user data before any move starts.

findings.closure: lstat every ref, reject symlinks, bind file SHA/bytes or directory device/inode from the frozen inventory, and preflight that no ref is within any released candidate path.
findings.evidence: Preserve refs are validated with Path.exists(), which follows symlinks, and only their path existence is rechecked after rename. The code does not bind lstat identity/content or globally reject a preserve ref that is another released candidate.
findings.impact: A symlink or replaced path can make the receipt claim an artifact remained preserved when only an external/replacement target exists; a later candidate move can invalidate an earlier reference.

review_mode: Read-only static review. The mover was not invoked and no paths were moved.
verified_safeguards: Current v2 selection is fail-closed under normal Python: it declares NO_ACTION_ALL_CANDIDATES_HELD and trash_authorized_now=false, which the current mover checks at lines 23-24. The mover was not run.

The current code binds release JSON to selection bytes, checks ignored/untracked status, checks candidate type/owner/device, rejects nested candidate paths, and compares preflight inode/device immediately before and after rename.
For the current selection, preserve references are disjoint from candidate paths and present at review time; this does not replace the generic lstat/reference checks requested above.
